config.title: List Virtualization

intro.title: List Virtualization
intro.body: In this lesson, you will build a Vue component that efficiently displays a large list of items using list virtualization. You will learn how to render only the visible items on the screen, which improves performance by reducing the number of DOM elements. The core concept involves calculating which items are in the viewport and dynamically updating the list as the user scrolls. You will use Vue's reactive state, computed properties, and event handlers to implement this technique in a single-file component.
intro.usecase: List virtualization is essential for handling large datasets in modern web applications. You'll see this pattern in social media feeds that display thousands of posts, e-commerce product catalogs with extensive filtering, and data dashboards showing real-time analytics. As a Vue developer, implementing virtualization ensures smooth scrolling and responsive interactions when building admin panels, financial transaction lists, or any interface where performance matters with massive datasets.

objectives: Implement a virtualized list component using Vue's composition API
Configure dynamic rendering based on scroll position and viewport height
Manipulate DOM elements to display only visible items within the viewport
Initialize and update state variables to track scroll position and visible range
Bind scroll event handlers to trigger re-rendering of visible items
Construct a reusable virtual list that maintains performance with large datasets
Integrate item height calculations to determine total scrollable container size

steps.title: Import Vue and required APIs (ref, computed, onMounted)
steps.instruction: Import Vue and the required composition APIs: ref, computed, and onMounted from 'vue'.
steps.hint: Use a single import statement to bring in all three APIs from the Vue package.
steps.analogousExample:
// Importing Vue composition APIs
import { ref, computed, onMounted } from 'vue'

steps.title: Create the main Vue component
steps.instruction: Create a Vue component named VirtualList using the script setup syntax. The component should export itself as the default export.
steps.hint: Use the <script setup> syntax and define a template section. The component should be ready to render content.
steps.analogousExample: // Example: basic Vue component with script setup
steps.expectedOutcome: A Vue component named VirtualList is created with script setup syntax and a basic template structure.
successCriteria: The component is named VirtualList, uses <script setup>, and has a template with a root div element.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're close. Make sure the component is named VirtualList and uses the script setup syntax with a template section.
steps.feedbackWrong: The component structure isn't quite right. Check that you're using <script setup> and have a template with a root element.

steps.title: Initialize the data array with sample items
steps.instruction: Inside the component's script setup section, create a reactive ref called 'items' that contains an array of sample data objects. Each object should have at least an 'id' and 'text' property.
steps.hint: Use the ref() function to create a reactive reference. Initialize it with an array of objects, where each object represents a list item.
steps.expectedOutcome: You'll have a reactive 'items' array containing sample data that will later be virtually rendered.
successCriteria: A reactive ref named 'items' is declared and initialized with an array of objects containing 'id' and 'text' properties.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're on the right track, but make sure 'items' is a reactive ref containing an array of objects with 'id' and 'text' properties.
steps.feedbackWrong: The 'items' array wasn't properly initialized. Remember to use ref() with an array of objects containing 'id' and 'text' properties.

steps.title: Initialize virtualization state variables
steps.instruction: Inside the component's script setup, create three reactive refs: scrollTop (initialized to 0), containerHeight (initialized to 400), and itemHeight (initialized to 50).
steps.hint: Use the ref function from Vue to create reactive references. Remember to import ref if not already imported (it is in the code).
steps.expectedOutcome: Three reactive ref variables are declared with initial values to track scroll position and viewport dimensions.
successCriteria: The code contains three ref declarations: scrollTop, containerHeight, and itemHeight with appropriate initial values.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You've created some refs, but check that you have all three: scrollTop, containerHeight, and itemHeight with appropriate initial values.
steps.feedbackWrong: The step requires creating three reactive refs for virtualization state. Try using ref() to create scrollTop, containerHeight, and itemHeight variables.

steps.title: Create computed property for visible range
steps.instruction: Create a computed property named 'visibleRange' that calculates startIndex and endIndex based on scrollTop, containerHeight, and itemHeight. Use the existing state variables and return an object with startIndex and endIndex.
steps.hint: Use the computed() function from Vue to create a reactive computed property. The calculation should use Math.floor for startIndex and Math.min for endIndex to ensure valid array bounds.
steps.expectedOutcome: A computed property named 'visibleRange' is created that returns an object with startIndex and endIndex calculated from scrollTop, containerHeight, and itemHeight.
successCriteria: The computed property 'visibleRange' exists and returns an object with startIndex and endIndex properties. The calculation uses scrollTop.value, containerHeight.value, itemHeight.value, and items.value.length.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're on the right track, but the computed property needs to return an object with both startIndex and endIndex. Make sure your calculation uses all the required state variables.
steps.feedbackWrong: The computed property is missing or incorrect. Remember to use computed() and calculate startIndex and endIndex based on scrollTop, containerHeight, and itemHeight.

steps.title: Create computed property for container padding
steps.instruction: Create a computed property named 'containerPadding' that returns an object with 'paddingTop' and 'paddingBottom' properties. Calculate paddingTop as startIndex * itemHeight.value and paddingBottom as (items.value.length - endIndex) * itemHeight.value.
steps.hint: Use the computed() function from Vue. The computed property should return an object with two numeric properties based on the visible range indices and item height.
steps.expectedOutcome: A computed property named 'containerPadding' is created that calculates the top and bottom padding needed to maintain proper scroll height for virtualized items.
successCriteria: The computed property 'containerPadding' exists and returns an object with 'paddingTop' and 'paddingBottom' properties calculated from the visible range indices and item height.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're on the right track, but check that your computed property returns an object with both 'paddingTop' and 'paddingBottom' properties, and that the calculations use the correct indices and item height.
steps.feedbackWrong: The container padding computed property is missing or incorrect. Remember to use computed() and return an object with paddingTop and paddingBottom based on the visible range indices and item height.

steps.title: Define the scroll handler function
steps.instruction: Create a function named handleScroll that updates the scrollTop ref when the container is scrolled.
steps.hint: Define a function that takes an event object and sets scrollTop.value to event.target.scrollTop.
steps.expectedOutcome: A handleScroll function is defined that updates scrollTop based on scroll events.
successCriteria: The handleScroll function is defined and updates scrollTop.value with the event's scrollTop property.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You've defined a function, but make sure it updates scrollTop.value with event.target.scrollTop.
steps.feedbackWrong: The scroll handler function is missing or doesn't properly update the scrollTop state.

steps.title: Set up the container element and scroll handler
steps.instruction: In the template, add a div element with a fixed height of 400px, vertical scroll overflow, and bind the handleScroll function to its scroll event.
steps.hint: Use the style attribute for height and overflow-y, and use @scroll to bind the handler.
steps.analogousExample: // Similar: a scrollable container with event binding
steps.expectedOutcome: A scrollable container div will be added to the template with the correct styling and scroll event binding.
successCriteria: The template contains a div with style="height: 400px; overflow-y: scroll" and @scroll="handleScroll".
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You've added a container, but check that it has the exact height (400px), vertical scroll overflow, and the scroll event handler binding.
steps.feedbackWrong: The container div is missing or doesn't have the required styling and event binding. Review the instruction.

steps.title: Render the visible items with proper positioning
steps.instruction: Inside the container div, add an inner div with the computed paddingTop style and render only the visible items using v-for.
steps.hint: Use the computed paddingTop value as a style attribute and iterate over visibleItems to create list items.

{{ item.text }}
steps.expectedOutcome: The container will display only the visible items with correct vertical positioning using dynamic padding.
successCriteria: An inner div with style="padding-top: {{ paddingTop }}px" is added inside the container, and visible items are rendered using v-for.
